articleBlocks: At first glance, this puzzle seemed to point towards a general category of 'Organizations'.
Clues like 'Assembly', 'Council', and 'Congress' are often associated with various types of groups and associations.
I was thinking about different clubs or societies.
But that theory broke when I saw 'Diet'.
That's not just a food plan; it's also a legislative body in some countries.
The 'Diet' clue forced me to rethink my initial understanding.
That's when I realized the common thread: these are all legislative bodies.
Each of these terms represents a different type of legislative body around the world.
The set is much cleaner than any initial broad guess.
Now it's clear: the puzzle highlights diverse forms of law-making assemblies.
Sometimes the oddball clue is the one that unlocks the answer.
Spotting that turning point is the key to solving these puzzles quickly.
solutionNarrative: Diet and Assembly first pulled me toward Organizations, so that was the first path I tested. It held together for a moment, but diet never really fit it. The more I pushed that first read, the more the board sounded stitched together instead of naturally solved.

The solve turned when I stopped treating diet as just another clue and asked what kind of thing each clue could really be describing. Once I made that shift, I was no longer thinking about Organizations; I was checking whether the earlier clues all behaved like parts of the same real set. That was when the answer became clear, because the remaining clues stopped feeling like separate trivia and started reinforcing the real category.
